artifacts.notes: Internet Archive item fr-lasance-missal-1937, uploaded 2023-01-27 by a private uploader, collections catechismbooks and folkscanomy_religion. Its item metadata was retrieved the same day and records 1879 page images at 300 ppi, page_number_confidence 98.20, and an autonomous machine text layer produced by tesseract 5.3.0-1-gd3a4 with `-l lat+eng+Latin`; it carries NO licence, rights, publisher, creator or date field, and its title is the bare identifier. The uploaded scan is stamped 'http://ccwatershed.org' at the foot of every page, 1865 times in this file; no Corpus Christi Watershed copyright notice appears anywhere in the bytes. 199,051 LF-terminated lines, valid UTF-8, no CR bytes. The file name asserts 1937 and is wrong; see the edition record. Two observations that are recorded and NOT relied on: the plate copyright lines scattered through the file OCR mostly as 'Copyright, 1936, by Benziger Brothers' but one, at line 67061 under the Corpus Christi plate, OCRs as 'Copyright, 1956'. A single scanned digit is not a printing date and 3 misread as 5 is an ordinary tesseract error, so this does not close `[the_appendix_exclusion]`, which asks for a title page or copyright leaf from a physical copy. It is written down because it points the same way as the internal evidence and because the next reader should not have to find it again.
artifacts.rights_basis: MIXED, WHICH IS WHY THESE EXACT BYTES ARE NOT TRACKED. The book itself is in the United States public domain by failure to renew, established at registration-number level for both registered editions in src/sources/inventories/lasance-new-roman-missal-rights-v1.toml. These bytes, however, also contain the appendix at printed pages 1298a-1298n, which is new matter first published after October 1954 under no registration that record could find, dated only by inference from the text, and EXCLUDED from any publication basis until the printing is dated from a physical copy. A single rights status cannot say 'public domain except for fourteen pages', so this record says unresolved over the whole and the affirmative basis is recorded on the derivative below, from which the excluded pages have been removed. Retrieval and redistribution are separate acts and this record is the first only. Nothing here rests on the Internet Archive: the item carries no license field at all, and availability and a successful download would not be a distribution basis if it did.

artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of a whole hand missal, 198,099 LF-terminated lines, landed as a plain source artifact and nothing more. It is deliberately NOT structured as liturgical records. The prior lt-hist corpus divided the same text into eleven markdown 'sections' whose only structural claim was a line range over the downloaded file, so a comparison of two such sections compares the scanner's disagreements rather than the liturgy's; nothing of that shape is reproduced here. Addressability by identity -- this collect, of this Mass -- belongs to passage records with real loci bound to physical line ranges over these exact bytes, which this schema already supports and which requires reading the pages rather than slicing the file. Until such a passage exists, this artifact is a finding aid.

WHAT SURVIVED THE APPENDIX EXCLUSION, STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER. The excised pages are gone, but two references to them remain in the body because they are not on those pages: at line 109815-109816 the sanctoral gives '31 May - Feast of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Queen / Page 1298g', and at lines 198080-198094 the general index carries an 'Appendix' block naming the Queenship, St Isidore the Farmer, St Frances Xavier Cabrini and St Pius X. Both are post-1954 insertions into the body of this printing, so the recorded exclusion by page range is not a complete account of the printing's new matter. They are retained because they are feast titles and page numbers -- a pointer, not the appendix's expression -- and because deleting body text the exclusion does not name would put an undisclosed editorial hand into the bytes. A reader must not take them as dating evidence and must not reconstruct the appendix from them.

OCR QUALITY. Measured here by scripts/_ocr_quality.py at a function-word share of en=0.24 and la=0.08 over 697,509 tokens, classified prose-english. The two figures must be read together and against a monolingual comparator: the book prints Latin and English in facing columns, so neither language can approach the 0.39-0.41 a keyed English text reaches, and their sum of 0.33 is the number that means the pages are prose. Individual lines are nonetheless corrupt in the ordinary ways -- 'Benriger' for Benziger at line 70, 'Missat' for Missal, running heads fused to body text -- and diacritics on the Latin survive unevenly. Quote from this artifact only through a checked passage, and do not rest a negative search on it: the raw-line modes establish absence of a string, not absence of a text.

IDENTITY. A printing of about 1955-56 of the 1945 revised edition, not the 1937 first edition; see the edition record. The 'http://ccwatershed.org' stamp at the foot of every scanned page is present 1865 times and is the scan host's watermark, carrying no notice and no claim.
artifacts.rights_basis: Public domain in the United States by failure to renew, on an affirmative record and on no other ground. The New Roman Missal was registered twice and neither registration was renewed in its twenty-eighth year: A 110108, copyright 15 July 1937, renewal window closed 15 July 1965; A 192159, copyright 1 November 1945, renewal window closed 1 November 1973. The finding was made at registration-number level across five bodies of the Copyright Office's published record and carries three positive controls drawn from the same OCR layer, so that the negative could be distinguished from a failed search; it is recorded in full, with its citations, its caveats and what would overturn it, at src/sources/inventories/lasance-new-roman-missal-rights-v1.toml. The 'Copyright, 1936, by Benziger Brothers' notice printed in the book is not disturbed and does not need to be: a notice establishes that a term began, and that record establishes that it ended. THE APPENDIX AT PRINTED PAGES 1298a-1298n IS NOT COVERED BY THAT BASIS AND IS NOT IN THESE BYTES. It is new matter first published after October 1954 under no registration found, dated only by inference, and it was removed by the transformation named below rather than carried across and disclaimed in prose. THE SCAN AND ITS TEXT LAYER ADD NOTHING FOR ANYONE TO OWN. A faithful mechanical reproduction of a public-domain work is not original authorship (Bridgeman Art Library v. Corel Corp., 36 F. Supp. 2d 191 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)), and machine optical character recognition adds no human authorship on top of it: this text layer was produced autonomously by tesseract 5.3.0, and there is no author to hold a right in it. That is the same reasoning this repository already applies to the CMAA facsimile at guidance/missals.md:325-346, with the difference that there it stood alone and disposed only of a licence, while here the underlying work has an affirmative basis of its own and the scan argument completes the case instead of substituting for one. NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the download succeeded, or that any host marks the scan public domain. guidance/sources.md:395-400 holds that availability and successful download are insufficient, the item in fact carries no licence field at all, and this basis would be unchanged if it carried one.

edition.notes: Bilingual throughout: the Latin of the Missale Romanum as revised through Benedict XV stands in one column and the compilers' English in the other, so `language = "en"` records the edition's own contribution and not the whole of what is printed. THIS EDITION IS NOT A TYPICAL EDITION AND NOT AN APPROVED ENGLISH EDITION OF ONE. It is a publisher's hand missal, and binding it as a witness to the Tridentine recension as promulgated would be an accuracy error that its rights position does nothing to prevent; for the Latin, cite work.catholic-church.missale-romanum and an edition of it. THE ONLY ARTIFACT HELD IS A LATER PRINTING OF THIS EDITION, NOT OF THE 1937 FIRST EDITION AND NOT OF THE 1945 IMPRESSION. The scanned copy is a printing of about 1955-56: at printed pages 1298a-1298n it carries an appendix stating that its feasts are 'additions to the 1945 Copyright edition', and it prints the Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary on 31 May and St Pius X on 3 September, neither of which could have been set before late 1954, while the body still carries the pre-1955 Holy Week with twelve prophecies on Holy Saturday and no renewal of baptismal promises. The uploaded item, the file name it is served under, and the prior lt-hist corpus all call it 1937; they are wrong, and anything citing this text as a 1937 witness is citing it wrongly. The base text is the 1945 revision, which is what this record names. The printing year itself is an inference from the text and is not established from a physical copy; see src/sources/inventories/lasance-new-roman-missal-rights-v1.toml `[the_local_artifact]` and `[the_appendix_exclusion]`.
edition.publication: The new Roman missal in Latin and English, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh. New York, Cincinnati [etc.]: Benziger Brothers, inc. Revised edition, copyright 1 November 1945, registered A 192159. The first edition of 1937 is a separate registration, A 110108, and is not this edition.
edition.title: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition

work.author: Francis Xavier Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh
work.description: A commercial hand missal compiled by Francis Xavier Lasance (1860-1946) and Francis Augustine Walsh, O.S.B. (1884-1938), published by Benziger Brothers and printed with the Latin of the Missale Romanum facing an English rendering, together with the compilers' own prefaces, instructions, meditations, saints' lives, glossary of liturgical terms and prayers for private devotion, and William R. Kelly's illustrated study plan 'Read Mass with the Priest'. It is a devotional book made for a layperson following the Mass, not an official liturgical book and not an approved English edition of any typical edition: its English is its compilers' and carries no authority of its own. It witnesses what an English-speaking Catholic of the mid twentieth century read alongside the altar book, and any use of it as evidence for the Roman Rite must say so. The work is named for its compilers rather than for the Church because the compilation, the arrangement and the English are theirs; the Latin it prints belongs to work.catholic-church.missale-romanum and is not made this work's by being reprinted here.
work.title: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English
